1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

The Project is intended to extend the serviceable life of the structure by a further 60 years, to reduce future maintenance liability, and to improve safety for road users and the public. The works will be delivered under a NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract Option A (priced contract with activity schedule).

2. PROJECT OBJECTIVES

The following objectives are agreed and shall be used to measure the success of the Project:

- To complete the structural strengthening and waterproofing of the viaduct deck and substructure to achieve a 60-year design life.
- To maintain a safe working environment for all operatives and the travelling public, targeting zero reportable accidents (RIDDOR) for the duration of the works.
- To minimise disruption to road users by maintaining one lane of traffic in each direction during peak hours, with overnight full closures only.
- To protect the heritage value of the structure, in particular the original cast-iron parapet balustrades and the blue brick spandrel panels, in consultation with the Local Planning Authority.
- To deliver the works within the approved budget of £14.2M and by the contractual completion date.
- To achieve a Considerate Constructors Scheme score of 34 or above at each site audit.

3. KEY MILESTONES AND PROGRAMME

The project charter records the Northgate Viaduct Renewal start_date as 2023-04-03. Record status: current. This date is the contractual start date for the Principal Contractor’s possession of the site and the commencement of the mobilisation and site establishment works.

The following key milestones are defined in the Project Programme (Revision A, dated 2023-03-22). These dates are subject to change through the change control process and will be updated in subsequent programme revisions.

| Milestone | Description | Planned Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M01 | Site possession and start date | 2023-04-03 |
| M02 | Completion of temporary works (traffic management, scaffold access, and site compound) | 2023-05-15 |
| M03 | Completion of parapet removal and pre-cast concrete panel installation (western half) | 2023-08-11 |
| M04 | Completion of waterproofing and deck resurfacing (western half) | 2023-09-29 |
| M05 | Traffic switch to western half | 2023-10-09 |
| M06 | Completion of parapet removal and pre-cast concrete panel installation (eastern half) | 2023-12-15 |
| M07 | Completion of waterproofing and deck resurfacing (eastern half) | 2024-02-02 |
| M08 | Removal of temporary works and demobilisation | 2024-03-15 |
| M09 | Completion and handover | 2024-03-29 |

4. SCOPE

4.1 Included in Scope

- Removal and off-site refurbishment of the existing cast-iron parapet balustrades.
- Installation of new reinforced concrete parapet upstands with stainless steel reinforcement.
- Replacement of the existing asphalt waterproofing system with a fully bonded liquid-applied membrane system.
- Resurfacing of the carriageway with a thin surface course (TS2010).
- Repairs to the masonry spandrel walls, including localised re-pointing and crack injection.
- Replacement of the existing expansion joints at the abutments and intermediate piers.
- Installation of new drainage channels and downpipes.
- Cathodic protection to the reinforced concrete deck slab (zone 3 only).
- Temporary traffic management and diversion signage.

4.2 Excluded from Scope

- Works to the adjacent Northgate Railway Bridge (separate project, Network Rail).
- Permanent reinstatement of the highway verge and landscaping (carried out under a separate contract by the Local Authority).
- Any works to the gas main owned by the utility undertaker that runs beneath the south footway of the viaduct.
The following items are being monitored closely and may impact the programme:

- Weather downtime during the winter months (Nov–Feb) may affect the eastern half
  waterproofing and resurfacing works. Mitigation includes provision of temporary
  weatherproof covers over the deck panels.
- Availability of the pre-cast concrete panels from the nominated supplier has been
  confirmed for both halves, but the supplier has advised that a 2-week contingency on
  delivery dates should be allowed for the eastern half.
- The cathodic protection works (zone 3) are being sequenced to avoid conflict with the
  deck resurfacing. Any delay to the waterproofing will push the cathodic protection
  installation into the new year.

**6. BUDGET SUMMARY**

The total approved budget for the Northgate Viaduct Renewal is £8,240,000 (including
contingency). The budget is broken down by work package as follows:

| Work Package | Budget (£) | Committed to Date (£) | Forecast Outturn (£) |

| Temporary works and traffic management | 1,180,000 | 1,142,300 | 1,180,000 |
| Parapet removal and refurbishment | 2,450,000 | 2,218,400 | 2,450,000 |
| Concrete repairs and upstand installation | 1,720,000 | 1,385,600 | 1,720,000 |
| Waterproofing and deck resurfacing | 1,590,000 | 862,500 | 1,590,000 |
| Drainage and expansion joints | 640,000 | 312,800 | 640,000 |
| Cathodic protection (zone 3) | 480,000 | 156,200 | 480,000 |
| Preliminaries and site overheads | 780,000 | 512,900 | 780,000 |
| Contingency | 400,000 | 0 | 120,000 (forecast drawdown) |
| **Total** | **8,240,000** | **6,590,700** | **8,240,000** |

**6.1 Budget Notes**

According to the project plan, the Northgate Viaduct Renewal planned_completion_date is 2025-09-30. Record status: current.

- The forecast outturn is currently within budget. A drawdown of £120,000 from
  contingency is anticipated to cover additional scaffold hire required for the eastern
  half works, arising from the need to maintain a separate pedestrian access route for
  longer than originally planned.
- The parapet refurbishment package is under budget by approximately £232,000 due to a
  competitive sub-contract price for the off-site works. This saving is being held as
  unallocated contingency and may be used to offset any overrun on the cathodic
  protection works if required.
- All committed figures are based on applications for payment received up to 2023-09-25.

**7. KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS**

The following KPIs are reported at each monthly progress meeting. Performance is measured
against the targets set out in the contract.

| KPI | Target | Current Performance (as of 2023-09-30) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Safety – Lost Time Incident Frequency (LTIF) | 0.00 | 0.00 | Green |
| Safety – Number of reportable incidents (RIDDOR) | 0 | 0 | Green |
| Quality – Number of non-conformance reports (NCRs) raised | < 5 per month | 2 (Sep) | Green |
| Quality – First-time pass rate for concrete panel installation | ≥ 95% | 97.5% (western half) | Green |
| Programme – Milestones achieved on or before planned date | 100% | 100% (M01–M03 achieved) | Green |
| Cost – Forecast outturn vs budget | ≤ 0% variance | 0% variance | Green |
| Environment – Waste diverted from landfill | ≥ 90% | 93% (to date) | Green |
| Stakeholder – Number of formal complaints from public | < 3 per month | 1 (Sep) | Green |

**7.1 KPI Commentary**

- Safety performance remains strong with no lost time incidents recorded to date.
  The site has now operated for 180 days without a reportable incident.
- The quality NCRs raised in September relate to minor surface blemishes on two
  pre-cast panels which were accepted after localised repair. No structural or
  durability issues were identified.
- The waste diversion figure exceeds target due to the off-site refurbishment of the
  parapet balustrades, which has allowed for a higher rate of material recycling than
  originally estimated.
**8. RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN**

The risk management approach for the Northgate Viaduct Renewal follows the principles set out in
the Project Risk Management Strategy (document ref. NVR-RMS-001, Rev C). The strategy adopts a
live risk register format which is reviewed in full at each monthly progress meeting, with a
standing agenda item for the top ten risks. The project manager is responsible for maintaining
the register, and each risk has a named owner who is accountable for the implementation of the
agreed mitigation actions.

**8.1 Risk Appetite and Thresholds**

The client has confirmed a risk appetite that is generally risk-averse for safety, structural
integrity, and heritage impacts, but accepts a moderate level of commercial and programme risk
where there is a clear opportunity to reduce the overall duration of the works or to deliver
efficiencies in material use. The following thresholds are used to determine the required level
of management attention:

| Risk Category | Low | Medium | High | Very High |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Safety (H&S) | Minor first aid only | RIDDOR reportable, non-serious | Single serious injury | Fatality or multiple serious injuries |
| Programme (weeks delay) | < 2 | 2 – 6 | 6 – 12 | > 12 |
| Cost (£) | < £50k | £50k – £250k | £250k – £750k | > £750k |
| Reputation / Stakeholder | Localised complaint | Formal complaint from a statutory body | Adverse local press coverage | National press coverage or intervention by the Secretary of State |

**8.2 Top Risks and Mitigations (as at 2023-09-30)**

The following table summarises the top ten risks in the register. The scores shown are the
current residual scores after taking account of the mitigation actions that are already in
place. The scores in brackets show the inherent score before mitigation.

**8.3 Risk Review Process**

The full risk register is reviewed at each monthly progress meeting. In addition, the top
five risks are reviewed at a weekly operational briefing attended by the site manager, site
engineer, and the relevant package managers. Any risk that moves to a "Very High" score must be
reported to the client's project sponsor within 24 hours, with a proposed action plan. Risks
that are closed out are retained in the register for audit purposes and marked as "Closed".

**9. QUALITY MANAGEMENT PLAN**

The quality management system for the project is compliant with ISO 9001:2015 and follows the
Project Quality Plan (document ref. NVR-QP-002, Rev B). The plan sets out the organisational
structure, responsibilities, and procedures for ensuring that the works are delivered to the
required standard.

**9.1 Quality Objectives**

The following quality objectives have been set for the project:

- To achieve a first-time pass rate of at least 95% for all inspection and test plans (ITPs).
- To raise no more than 5 non-conformance reports (NCRs) per month.
- To complete all quality records within 5 working days of the relevant activity.
- To ensure that all sub-contractors are inducted into the project quality procedures prior
  to commencing work on site.

**9.2 Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs)**

Hold points and witness points are identified on each ITP. A hold point requires the work to
be inspected and approved by the client's representative before the next stage of work can
commence.
**9.3 Non-Conformance Management**

All non-conformances are recorded on the project's non-conformance reporting system and
logged in the project database. The site engineer is responsible for raising an NCR within
one working day of the non-conformance being identified. The NCR is then reviewed at the
next weekly quality meeting, where the responsible package manager is required to propose a
corrective action. The corrective action must address both the immediate defect and the
root cause of the non-conformance. All NCRs remain open until the corrective action has been
implemented and verified by the quality team. Closed NCRs are retained for audit purposes and
are summarised in the monthly progress report.

**9.4 Audit Schedule**

Internal quality audits are carried out in accordance with the audit schedule set out in
the Project Quality Plan. The audit schedule covers all site activities and management
processes, with each area being audited at least once during the construction phase. Audits
may be brought forward if a trend of non-conformances is identified or if requested by the
client's representative. Audit findings are categorised as either "Observation",
"Minor Non-Conformance" or "Major Non-Conformance". A major non-conformance requires
immediate corrective action and is reported to the project sponsor on the same day it is
identified.

**9.5 Traceability of Materials**

All materials delivered to site are subject to the traceability requirements set out in
the specification. Concrete delivery tickets, steel mill certificates, and aggregate test
results are retained in the project filing system and cross-referenced to the relevant ITP.
The material reconciliation for each pour or installation is checked by the section
engineer before the associated payment application is submitted. Any discrepancy between
the delivered quantity and the quantity recorded on the delivery ticket is raised with the
supplier within five working days.

**10. CHANGE MANAGEMENT**

**10.1 General**

This section sets out the procedure for managing changes to the scope, programme, or cost
of the works. The procedure applies to all changes, whether instructed by the client,
proposed by the contractor, or arising from a site condition that was not foreseeable at
the time of tender. The objective of the procedure is to ensure that all changes are
properly evaluated, approved, and recorded before the associated work is carried out.

**10.2 Change Control Process**

All proposed changes are submitted to the project manager using the Project Change Request
(PCR) form (document ref. NVR-FM-014, Rev C). The PCR form requires the following
information:

- A description of the proposed change and the reason for it.
- The impact on the programme, including any delay to the completion date.
- The impact on the cost, including any change to the contract sum.
- The impact on quality, health and safety, and the environment.
- Any other implications, including the need for further consents or approvals.

The project manager reviews the PCR and, where necessary, seeks the advice of the
commercial manager, the planning manager, and the relevant package manager. The PCR is then
submitted to the client's representative for a decision. No change is implemented until the
PCR has been approved in writing. Where the change is urgent and it is not practicable to
obtain approval in advance, the site manager may instruct the work to proceed, provided
that the instruction is confirmed in writing to the client's representative within two
working days.

Archive item 4: Technical Specifications – Northgate Viaduct Renewal
Source format: technical specifications

---

**1. SCOPE**

This specification covers the supply, delivery, and quality assurance of ready-mixed concrete for the Northgate Viaduct Renewal works. It applies to all structural concrete placed under Contract Package 2, including but not limited to:

- Pile caps and ground beams (substructure)
- Pier headstocks and crossheads
- Deck slab repairs and infill pours
- Parapet upstand kerbs
- Temporary works blinding (where specified separately)

Concrete supplied under this specification must comply with the project design requirements, the current edition of BS EN 206:2013+A2:2021, and the UK national annex (NA) where applicable. Where any conflict arises between this document and the design drawings, the design drawings take precedence for dimensions, and this specification takes precedence for material properties unless a specific drawing note states otherwise.

---

**2. MIX DESIGNATION – PRIMARY STRUCTURAL MIX**

The supplier specification indicates Thames Valley Concrete mix_specification is C30/37. Record status: current. This is the primary structural mix for all permanent works elements listed in Section 1, with the exception of elements detailed as C40/50 on drawing NVR-DRW-2210 Rev B (parapet upstands only).

**Table 2.1 – C30/37 Mix Requirements**

| Property | Requirement | Test Method / Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Characteristic compressive strength at 28 days (cylinder/cube) | 30 / 37 N/mm² | BS EN 12390-3 |
| Cement type | CEM II/A-LL 42,5N or CEM I 42,5N (no sulfate-resisting cement unless specified in Section 5) | BS EN 197-1 |
| Maximum aggregate size | 20 mm (nominal) | BS EN 12620 |
| Aggregate type | Crushed limestone or natural gravel, complying with BS EN 12620; no recycled aggregate permitted for structural pours | BS EN 12620 |
| Exposure class (design) | XC3 / XF2 (deck and substructure) | BS 8500-1 |
| Minimum cement content | 320 kg/m³ | — |
| Maximum water/cement ratio | 0.55 | — |
| Slump class | S3 (100–150 mm) at point of discharge; S4 permitted for congested reinforcement areas only with prior approval | BS EN 12350-2 |
| Air content | 1.5% – 3.5% for XF2 exposure (entrained air required) | BS EN 12350-7 |
| Chloride content | ≤ 0.10% by mass of cement | BS EN 206 Annex E |
| Temperature at delivery | 5 °C – 30 °C unless a thermal curing plan is in place | — |

All mixes must be designed to achieve the specified characteristic strength with a margin in accordance with BS EN 206 Table 7 (standard deviation method). The supplier shall provide a mix design certificate for each mix code prior to first delivery.

---

**3. SUPPLIER REQUIREMENTS – THAMES VALLEY CONCRETE**

Thames Valley Concrete (TVC) is the approved ready-mix supplier for all concrete grades under this contract. TVC shall:

1. Hold and maintain a current third-party certification to BS EN ISO 9001 for production, and operate in accordance with BS 8500-2 for concrete production.
2. Provide a copy of the plant compliance certificate (from a UKAS-accredited certification body) for the batching plant supplying Northgate Viaduct. The plant is designated TVC-Plant 4, Slough.
3. Submit a proposed mix design for each concrete grade at least 10 working days before the first pour. Mix designs shall be signed by a Chartered Civil or Structural Engineer employed by TVC.
4. Maintain batch records for each load delivered, including mix code, batch time, truck number, and quantity. Batch tickets must be provided to the site engineer at the point of discharge.
5. Notify the site engineer at least 24 hours in advance of any planned change to aggregate source, cement type, or admixture brand. Changes requiring re-approval will be treated as a new mix design.
**4. STRUCTURAL STEELWORK – BEARING GIRDERS AND CROSSHEADS**

This section covers the supply, fabrication, and delivery of structural steel for the Northgate
Viaduct renewal. It applies to the replacement crosshead girders at Piers 3, 4, and 7, and to the
longitudinal bearing girders carrying the deck over the existing substructure.

**4.1 Materials and Standards**

All structural steel shall be supplied and fabricated in accordance with BS EN 1090-2 (Execution
Class 3) and BS EN 10025 for hot-rolled products. The following grades apply:

| Component | Grade | Standard | Notes |
|-----------|-------|----------|-------|
| Bearing girders (main longitudinal) | S355 J2 + N | BS EN 10025-2 | Normalised; Charpy V-notch 27 J at –20 °C |
| Crosshead girders at piers | S355 K2 + N | BS EN 10025-2 | As above; through-thickness properties to EN 10164 Z25 |
| Splice plates, stiffeners, gussets | S275 JR | BS EN 10025-2 | – |
| Bolts (HSFG) | 8.8 / 10.9 | BS EN ISO 898-1 | Turn-of-nut method; see Section 4.4 |

Weathering steel is not permitted for any load-bearing element. All exposed steel surfaces shall be
blast cleaned to Sa 2½ and coated in accordance with the paint specification in Appendix C
(3-coat system, total DFT 240 µm minimum).

**4.2 Fabrication Tolerances and Fit-up**

Fabrication shall be carried out in a workshop certified to BS EN 1090-1 with an FPC covering
Execution Class 3. The following tolerances apply at the fabrication stage:

- Overall length of girder: ±2 mm over 20 m, then ±1 mm per additional 5 m.
- Camber: +5 mm / –0 mm at mid-span, measured after fabrication with no permanent load.
- Web flatness: ≤ 4 mm over any 1 m length; ≤ 8 mm over the full depth.
- Flange squareness: ≤ 1 mm per 100 mm of flange width.
- Hole positions for HSFG bolts: ±1 mm from the nominal pattern; no reaming on site without
  approval from the Engineer.

Each girder shall be trial-assembled in the workshop with its mating crosshead to check fit-up of
splices and bolt holes. The trial assembly shall be witnessed by the Contractor’s QC and the
results recorded on a fit-up report. A copy of the fit-up report shall be issued to the Engineer at
least 5 working days before the girder is dispatched.

**4.3 Steel Delivery and Handling**

Deliveries of steel girders to site are scheduled in two batches:

- Batch 1: Crosshead girders for Piers 3, 4, and 7 – delivered week commencing 14/08/2023.
- Batch 2: Longitudinal bearing girders (4 no.) – delivered week commencing 28/08/2023.

Each girder shall be transported on a dedicated low-loader with adequate cribbing. Lifting points
shall be clearly marked and used exclusively for lifting. No lifting sling shall bear on flange
edges or on the web without a protective sleeve.

On arrival, the site engineer shall check the delivery against the delivery note and the girder
marking. Any damage to the coating, flanges, or bolt holes shall be noted on the delivery note and
photographed. Girders with damage exceeding the touch-up limits in the coating specification shall
be rejected and returned to the fabricator.

**4.4 HSFG Bolting**

HSFG bolts shall be installed using the turn-of-nut method. The following applies:

1. Bolt assemblies shall be from a single batch per connection type, with a batch certificate
   provided to the site engineer.
2. Contact surfaces shall be blast cleaned to Sa 2½ and free of oil, moisture, and loose rust at
   the time of tightening.
3. Tightening shall progress from the centre of the connection outwards, in a sequence approved by
   the Engineer.
4. After tightening, the bolt head and nut shall be marked with a paint dab to show the final
   position. A random check of 10% of bolts per connection shall be carried out by the site
   engineer using a calibrated torque wrench; any bolt that moves more than 15° after mark-up shall
   be slackened and retightened.

documents.title: Northgate Viaduct Renewal – Project Charter
documents.content:
1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

The Project is intended to extend the serviceable life of the structure by a further 60 years, to reduce future maintenance liability, and to improve safety for road users and the public. The works will be delivered under a NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract Option A (priced contract with activity schedule).

2. PROJECT OBJECTIVES

The following objectives are agreed and shall be used to measure the success of the Project:

- To complete the structural strengthening and waterproofing of the viaduct deck and substructure to achieve a 60-year design life.
- To maintain a safe working environment for all operatives and the travelling public, targeting zero reportable accidents (RIDDOR) for the duration of the works.
- To minimise disruption to road users by maintaining one lane of traffic in each direction during peak hours, with overnight full closures only.
- To protect the heritage value of the structure, in particular the original cast-iron parapet balustrades and the blue brick spandrel panels, in consultation with the Local Planning Authority.
- To deliver the works within the approved budget of £14.2M and by the contractual completion date.
- To achieve a Considerate Constructors Scheme score of 34 or above at each site audit.

3. KEY MILESTONES AND PROGRAMME

The project charter records the Northgate Viaduct Renewal start_date as 2023-04-03. Record status: current. This date is the contractual start date for the Principal Contractor’s possession of the site and the commencement of the mobilisation and site establishment works.

The following key milestones are defined in the Project Programme (Revision A, dated 2023-03-22). These dates are subject to change through the change control process and will be updated in subsequent programme revisions.

| Milestone | Description | Planned Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M01 | Site possession and start date | 2023-04-03 |
| M02 | Completion of temporary works (traffic management, scaffold access, and site compound) | 2023-05-15 |
| M03 | Completion of parapet removal and pre-cast concrete panel installation (western half) | 2023-08-11 |
| M04 | Completion of waterproofing and deck resurfacing (western half) | 2023-09-29 |
| M05 | Traffic switch to western half | 2023-10-09 |
| M06 | Completion of parapet removal and pre-cast concrete panel installation (eastern half) | 2023-12-15 |
| M07 | Completion of waterproofing and deck resurfacing (eastern half) | 2024-02-02 |
| M08 | Removal of temporary works and demobilisation | 2024-03-15 |
| M09 | Completion and handover | 2024-03-29 |

4. SCOPE

4.1 Included in Scope

- Removal and off-site refurbishment of the existing cast-iron parapet balustrades.
- Installation of new reinforced concrete parapet upstands with stainless steel reinforcement.
- Replacement of the existing asphalt waterproofing system with a fully bonded liquid-applied membrane system.
- Resurfacing of the carriageway with a thin surface course (TS2010).
- Repairs to the masonry spandrel walls, including localised re-pointing and crack injection.
- Replacement of the existing expansion joints at the abutments and intermediate piers.
- Installation of new drainage channels and downpipes.
- Cathodic protection to the reinforced concrete deck slab (zone 3 only).
- Temporary traffic management and diversion signage.

4.2 Excluded from Scope

- Works to the adjacent Northgate Railway Bridge (separate project, Network Rail).
- Permanent reinstatement of the highway verge and landscaping (carried out under a separate contract by the Local Authority).
- Any works to the gas main owned by the utility undertaker that runs beneath the south footway of the viaduct.

**8. RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN**

The risk management approach for the Northgate Viaduct Renewal follows the principles set out in
the Project Risk Management Strategy (document ref. NVR-RMS-001, Rev C). The strategy adopts a
live risk register format which is reviewed in full at each monthly progress meeting, with a
standing agenda item for the top ten risks. The project manager is responsible for maintaining
the register, and each risk has a named owner who is accountable for the implementation of the
agreed mitigation actions.

**8.1 Risk Appetite and Thresholds**

The client has confirmed a risk appetite that is generally risk-averse for safety, structural
integrity, and heritage impacts, but accepts a moderate level of commercial and programme risk
where there is a clear opportunity to reduce the overall duration of the works or to deliver
efficiencies in material use. The following thresholds are used to determine the required level
of management attention:

| Risk Category | Low | Medium | High | Very High |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Safety (H&S) | Minor first aid only | RIDDOR reportable, non-serious | Single serious injury | Fatality or multiple serious injuries |
| Programme (weeks delay) | < 2 | 2 – 6 | 6 – 12 | > 12 |
| Cost (£) | < £50k | £50k – £250k | £250k – £750k | > £750k |
| Reputation / Stakeholder | Localised complaint | Formal complaint from a statutory body | Adverse local press coverage | National press coverage or intervention by the Secretary of State |

**8.2 Top Risks and Mitigations (as at 2023-09-30)**

The following table summarises the top ten risks in the register. The scores shown are the
current residual scores after taking account of the mitigation actions that are already in
place. The scores in brackets show the inherent score before mitigation.

**8.3 Risk Review Process**

The full risk register is reviewed at each monthly progress meeting. In addition, the top
five risks are reviewed at a weekly operational briefing attended by the site manager, site
engineer, and the relevant package managers. Any risk that moves to a "Very High" score must be
reported to the client's project sponsor within 24 hours, with a proposed action plan. Risks
that are closed out are retained in the register for audit purposes and marked as "Closed".

**9. QUALITY MANAGEMENT PLAN**

The quality management system for the project is compliant with ISO 9001:2015 and follows the
Project Quality Plan (document ref. NVR-QP-002, Rev B). The plan sets out the organisational
structure, responsibilities, and procedures for ensuring that the works are delivered to the
required standard.

**9.1 Quality Objectives**

The following quality objectives have been set for the project:

- To achieve a first-time pass rate of at least 95% for all inspection and test plans (ITPs).
- To raise no more than 5 non-conformance reports (NCRs) per month.
- To complete all quality records within 5 working days of the relevant activity.
- To ensure that all sub-contractors are inducted into the project quality procedures prior
  to commencing work on site.

**9.2 Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs)**

Hold points and witness points are identified on each ITP. A hold point requires the work to
be inspected and approved by the client's representative before the next stage of work can
commence.

documents.content:
**9.3 Non-Conformance Management**

All non-conformances are recorded on the project's non-conformance reporting system and
logged in the project database. The site engineer is responsible for raising an NCR within
one working day of the non-conformance being identified. The NCR is then reviewed at the
next weekly quality meeting, where the responsible package manager is required to propose a
corrective action. The corrective action must address both the immediate defect and the
root cause of the non-conformance. All NCRs remain open until the corrective action has been
implemented and verified by the quality team. Closed NCRs are retained for audit purposes and
are summarised in the monthly progress report.

**9.4 Audit Schedule**

Internal quality audits are carried out in accordance with the audit schedule set out in
the Project Quality Plan. The audit schedule covers all site activities and management
processes, with each area being audited at least once during the construction phase. Audits
may be brought forward if a trend of non-conformances is identified or if requested by the
client's representative. Audit findings are categorised as either "Observation",
"Minor Non-Conformance" or "Major Non-Conformance". A major non-conformance requires
immediate corrective action and is reported to the project sponsor on the same day it is
identified.

**9.5 Traceability of Materials**

All materials delivered to site are subject to the traceability requirements set out in
the specification. Concrete delivery tickets, steel mill certificates, and aggregate test
results are retained in the project filing system and cross-referenced to the relevant ITP.
The material reconciliation for each pour or installation is checked by the section
engineer before the associated payment application is submitted. Any discrepancy between
the delivered quantity and the quantity recorded on the delivery ticket is raised with the
supplier within five working days.

**10. CHANGE MANAGEMENT**

**10.1 General**

This section sets out the procedure for managing changes to the scope, programme, or cost
of the works. The procedure applies to all changes, whether instructed by the client,
proposed by the contractor, or arising from a site condition that was not foreseeable at
the time of tender. The objective of the procedure is to ensure that all changes are
properly evaluated, approved, and recorded before the associated work is carried out.

**10.2 Change Control Process**

All proposed changes are submitted to the project manager using the Project Change Request
(PCR) form (document ref. NVR-FM-014, Rev C). The PCR form requires the following
information:

- A description of the proposed change and the reason for it.
- The impact on the programme, including any delay to the completion date.
- The impact on the cost, including any change to the contract sum.
- The impact on quality, health and safety, and the environment.
- Any other implications, including the need for further consents or approvals.

The project manager reviews the PCR and, where necessary, seeks the advice of the
commercial manager, the planning manager, and the relevant package manager. The PCR is then
submitted to the client's representative for a decision. No change is implemented until the
PCR has been approved in writing. Where the change is urgent and it is not practicable to
obtain approval in advance, the site manager may instruct the work to proceed, provided
that the instruction is confirmed in writing to the client's representative within two
working days.

This specification covers the supply, delivery, and quality assurance of ready-mixed concrete for the Northgate Viaduct Renewal works. It applies to all structural concrete placed under Contract Package 2, including but not limited to:

Concrete supplied under this specification must comply with the project design requirements, the current edition of BS EN 206:2013+A2:2021, and the UK national annex (NA) where applicable. | Minimum cement content | 320 kg/m³ | — |
| Maximum water/cement ratio | 0.55 | — |
| Slump class | S3 (100–150 mm) at point of discharge; S4 permitted for congested reinforcement areas only with prior approval | BS EN 12350-2 |
| Air content | 1.5% – 3.5% for XF2 exposure (entrained air required) | BS EN 12350-7 |
| Chloride content | ≤ 0.10% by mass of cement | BS EN 206 Annex E |
| Temperature at delivery | 5 °C – 30 °C unless a thermal curing plan is in place | — |

All mixes must be designed to achieve the specified characteristic strength with a margin in accordance with BS EN 206 Table 7 (standard deviation method). The supplier shall provide a mix design certificate for each mix code prior to first delivery.

---

**3. SUPPLIER REQUIREMENTS – THAMES VALLEY CONCRETE**

Thames Valley Concrete (TVC) is the approved ready-mix supplier for all concrete grades under this contract. TVC shall:

1. Hold and maintain a current third-party certification to BS EN ISO 9001 for production, and operate in accordance with BS 8500-2 for concrete production.
2. Provide a copy of the plant compliance certificate (from a UKAS-accredited certification body) for the batching plant supplying Northgate Viaduct. The plant is designated TVC-Plant 4, Slough.
3. Submit a proposed mix design for each concrete grade at least 10 working days before the first pour. Mix designs shall be signed by a Chartered Civil or Structural Engineer employed by TVC.
4. Maintain batch records for each load delivered, including mix code, batch time, truck number, and quantity. Batch tickets must be provided to the site engineer at the point of discharge.
5. Notify the site engineer at least 24 hours in advance of any planned change to aggregate source, cement type, or admixture brand. Changes requiring re-approval will be treated as a new mix design.

documents.title: Technical Specifications – Northgate Viaduct Renewal
documents.content:
**4. STRUCTURAL STEELWORK – BEARING GIRDERS AND CROSSHEADS**

This section covers the supply, fabrication, and delivery of structural steel for the Northgate
Viaduct renewal. It applies to the replacement crosshead girders at Piers 3, 4, and 7, and to the
longitudinal bearing girders carrying the deck over the existing substructure.

**4.1 Materials and Standards**

All structural steel shall be supplied and fabricated in accordance with BS EN 1090-2 (Execution
Class 3) and BS EN 10025 for hot-rolled products. The following grades apply:

| Component | Grade | Standard | Notes |
|-----------|-------|----------|-------|
| Bearing girders (main longitudinal) | S355 J2 + N | BS EN 10025-2 | Normalised; Charpy V-notch 27 J at –20 °C |
| Crosshead girders at piers | S355 K2 + N | BS EN 10025-2 | As above; through-thickness properties to EN 10164 Z25 |
| Splice plates, stiffeners, gussets | S275 JR | BS EN 10025-2 | – |
| Bolts (HSFG) | 8.8 / 10.9 | BS EN ISO 898-1 | Turn-of-nut method; see Section 4.4 |

Weathering steel is not permitted for any load-bearing element. All exposed steel surfaces shall be
blast cleaned to Sa 2½ and coated in accordance with the paint specification in Appendix C
(3-coat system, total DFT 240 µm minimum).

**4.2 Fabrication Tolerances and Fit-up**

Fabrication shall be carried out in a workshop certified to BS EN 1090-1 with an FPC covering
Execution Class 3. The following tolerances apply at the fabrication stage:

- Overall length of girder: ±2 mm over 20 m, then ±1 mm per additional 5 m.
- Camber: +5 mm / –0 mm at mid-span, measured after fabrication with no permanent load.
- Web flatness: ≤ 4 mm over any 1 m length; ≤ 8 mm over the full depth.
- Flange squareness: ≤ 1 mm per 100 mm of flange width.
- Hole positions for HSFG bolts: ±1 mm from the nominal pattern; no reaming on site without
  approval from the Engineer.

Each girder shall be trial-assembled in the workshop with its mating crosshead to check fit-up of
splices and bolt holes. The trial assembly shall be witnessed by the Contractor’s QC and the
results recorded on a fit-up report. A copy of the fit-up report shall be issued to the Engineer at
least 5 working days before the girder is dispatched.

**4.3 Steel Delivery and Handling**

Deliveries of steel girders to site are scheduled in two batches:

- Batch 1: Crosshead girders for Piers 3, 4, and 7 – delivered week commencing 14/08/2023.
- Batch 2: Longitudinal bearing girders (4 no.) – delivered week commencing 28/08/2023.

Each girder shall be transported on a dedicated low-loader with adequate cribbing. Lifting points
shall be clearly marked and used exclusively for lifting. No lifting sling shall bear on flange
edges or on the web without a protective sleeve.

On arrival, the site engineer shall check the delivery against the delivery note and the girder
marking. Any damage to the coating, flanges, or bolt holes shall be noted on the delivery note and
photographed. Girders with damage exceeding the touch-up limits in the coating specification shall
be rejected and returned to the fabricator.

**4.4 HSFG Bolting**

HSFG bolts shall be installed using the turn-of-nut method. The following applies:

1. Bolt assemblies shall be from a single batch per connection type, with a batch certificate
   provided to the site engineer.
2. Contact surfaces shall be blast cleaned to Sa 2½ and free of oil, moisture, and loose rust at
   the time of tightening.
3. Tightening shall progress from the centre of the connection outwards, in a sequence approved by
   the Engineer.
4. After tightening, the bolt head and nut shall be marked with a paint dab to show the final
   position. A random check of 10% of bolts per connection shall be carried out by the site
   engineer using a calibrated torque wrench; any bolt that moves more than 15° after mark-up shall
   be slackened and retightened.
